sn22.54:1.2: _Bījajāta_ are not “kinds of seeds” but “plants grown from seeds” ([pli-tv-bu-vb-pc11](): _Bhūtagāmo nāma pañca bījajātāni_). Similarly, _mūlabīja_ is not “root-seeds” but “plants grown from roots” such as ginger or turmeric. The SN commentary and the Vinaya commentary are not entirely in agreement on this point.
sn22.54:1.4: _Bījajāta_ are not “kinds of seeds” but “plants grown from seeds” ([pli-tv-bu-vb-pc11](): _Bhūtagāmo nāma pañca bījajātāni_). Similarly, _mūlabīja_ is not “root-seeds” but “plants grown from roots” such as ginger or turmeric. The SN commentary and the Vinaya commentary are not entirely in agreement on this point.
sn22.54:1.5: _Sukhasayita_ is sometimes understood as “well planted”, but how can it be planted when there is no soil? It is explained by the commentary as “well-kept”, literally “well laid by”.
sn22.54:1.11: Pali uses the same word _viññāṇaṭṭhiti_ for the seven “planes of consciousness” (realms of rebirth, [an7.44](), [dn15:33.1]()) as for the four “grounds for consciousness”, namely the other four aggregates on which consciousness is based.
